findings.claim: The declared objective is final predicted target affinity primary with validity and strain secondary, coordinate control only; the reward view is the endpoint pointcloud with a detached Hungarian endpoint mean squared distance and native endpoint VJP, so no affinity-head derivative or extra model forward is available as evidence.

The learning window is [0,0.5] with observed score times on a 0.01 grid, and recorded affinities were removed with an equal score prior; therefore no decoded terminal affinity labels exist in the supplied evidence and last-record or survival credit cannot be presented as final affinity benefit.

Terminal metadata show one future-resampling node per batch at terminal index 99 (score time 0.99, state time 1.0) across 14 batches, so the observed support ends at 0.49 while terminal credit is computed beyond it; the immediate-selection versus descendant-credit comparison is unavailable without decoded terminal labels.

Ancestral coverage is thin: 349 of 700 batch nodes have fewer than 3 ancestors and 531 have fewer than 6, with at most 2 teachers per batch, so survival/quality credit is dominated by nodes with little ancestral support and is subject to survivor bias.

The information audit reports 14 independent batches and states its metrics are not the full score-weighted reward or its FLOWR Jacobian, that nonnegative excess distance is by construction rather than a causal affinity effect, and that teacher score correlations are observational and not a validated affinity predictor.

Among endpoint effects, shape_yy shows the strongest and most reproducible integrated signal (negative, q about 1.5e-5, positive batch fraction 0.0) and shape_xx is also negative with q about 8e-4 and positive batch fraction 0.07, whereas global_centroid_x and global_centroid_z are not significant (q about 0.26 and 0.48) with mixed batch signs.

global_centroid_y is negative and significant (q about 0.014) but with positive batch fraction only 0.21, and shape_zz is marginal (q about 0.067) with positive batch fraction 0.29; these are weaker and less reproducible than the shape_xx/shape_yy signals.

The curve-support selection retained 24 features under a rule requiring absolute integrated z at least 0.1, batch direction fraction at least about 0.857, exclusion of a scale floor and q below 0.05, with a fidelity rule of relative RMSE at most 0.35, zero strong sign-conflict nodes and quiet-node large-fit fraction at most 0.1; the per-feature fidelity contents were only summarized and not read.

hypotheses.direction: Oppose the negative shape_xx/shape_yy integrated endpoint contrast while leaving global centroid translation free.
hypotheses.falsifier: A batch-level counterexample in which shape_xx or shape_yy integrated contrast flips sign in a majority of independent batches, or a fidelity audit showing strong sign conflicts for those features.
hypotheses.observable: Integrated endpoint contrast z for shape_xx and shape_yy over the observed window, with per-batch sign fraction.
hypotheses.scope: Endpoint coordinate contrast over the observed score-time window [0,0.5]; not a terminal affinity label.
hypotheses.statement: A coordinate rule that reduces the negative shape_xx and shape_yy endpoint contrast (i.e., opposes the observed negative integrated direction) is a higher-priority direction than one targeting global centroid translation, because the shape signals are the only endpoint effects with both strong multiplicity-adjusted significance and near-unanimous batch direction.

hypotheses.direction: Do not convert survival or last-record credit into a coordinate reward direction.
hypotheses.falsifier: Delivery of decoded terminal affinity labels with adequate ancestral coverage that shows survival credit tracking final affinity.
hypotheses.observable: Ancestor-count distribution per node and the presence or absence of decoded terminal affinity labels.
hypotheses.statement: Because ancestral coverage is thin and terminal labels are undecoded, any survival- or last-record-based credit should be treated as a diagnostic of cohort composition rather than as evidence of within-path affinity improvement.

limitations: No decoded terminal affinity labels are supplied; the immediate-selection versus descendant-credit comparison and any final-affinity benefit claim are unavailable.
The curve-fidelity audit contents were delivered only as a container summary; per-feature fidelity values were not read, so no per-feature fit-fidelity claim is made.

The information audit explicitly states its metrics are not the full score-weighted reward or its FLOWR Jacobian and that teacher score correlations are observational, so no causal affinity or neural-module causation claim is made.
Turnover, increment and regional tables were not read in this pass; no within-path versus cohort-composition conclusion is asserted.
Temperatures are immutable task parameters and no temperature edit is proposed or evaluated.
